column2: My program is five forms joined by buttons, plus one text file that saves each pupil.
I know what a form, a control, a property and IntelliSense are.
My program is five forms joined by buttons, plus one text file that saves each pupil.
Solution Explorer lists my forms and Global.cs, on the right of Visual Studio.
Double-clicking a form opens the Design tab, and View Code opens the code tab.
The green Start arrow runs my program.
The red square stops my program.
Every chapter has the same shape, and the home page shows me my next job.
A chapter is a row of parts, each part is a few screens, and each screen has one job.
The big button at the bottom ticks a screen off and moves me on.
The home page lists every part in order, I tick what I have done, and I open the first part that is not ticked.
Three rules run through every chapter of this guide.
The guide shows the names Mr Gartland gave his controls, and I use the names I gave mine.
To find a control's name, I click it once in the Design tab.
The name sits beside Name at the top of the Properties window.
When I type the first letters of a name, IntelliSense lists the names in my program and Tab finishes it.
I type the first letters of a name on a new line.
The list pops up with every matching name in my program.
Tab types the name for me, spelt right.
I cannot copy code from the guide, I type it, and I read each line as I type it.
I have tried to copy a line and seen the guide refuse.
A red wiggly line means Visual Studio does not understand that line, and the Error List takes me to it.
Build Solution checks every line, and Build succeeded at the bottom left means I can run it.
Before I start, I check Global.cs, the test panel on the data entry form and the data entry Load event.
This part is where YOUR test becomes different from MINE. You choose the look, then save your pictures where the program can find them.
The idea of the test stays the same, but the look of mine is my own choice.
The idea of the test stays the same, but I choose my own shape, pictures, swapping boxes and timing.
My two or three pictures are saved in a folder called Images inside bin and then Debug.
This part adds frmTest and puts everything on it: twelve picture boxes, a score panel and two timers.
A new form called frmTest is in Solution Explorer, with a title label and an instructions label.
Twelve picture boxes sit on frmTest, named pbx1 to pbx12 in reading order, each stretching its picture.
The score panel holds the Start button, the score, the time left, the pupil's name and the ? button.
I know what tmrSwap and tmrCountdown are for before I add them.
Two timers called tmrSwap and tmrCountdown sit in the grey strip under the form, each with Interval 1000.
This part types two lines at the top of frmTest's code, then its Load event.
Two lines at the top of frmTest's code make the countdown start at 10 and make room for a list of picture boxes.
The Load event of frmTest shows the pupil's name and puts all twelve picture boxes into one list.
This part makes PictureBox_Click. It runs when any of the twelve boxes is clicked.
One piece of code, PictureBox_Click, runs for any of the twelve boxes, and it finds out which box was clicked.
A click on the winning picture adds one to the score, any other picture takes one off, and the picture hides.
This part types the code behind Start, tmrSwap and tmrCountdown. That is the whole test running.
When Start is clicked, each of the twelve boxes is given its first picture, a mix of winners and losers.
I see how one loop joins all twelve boxes to PictureBox_Click.
A loop joins every box to PictureBox_Click, both timers start, and the Start button switches itself off.
Each tick of tmrSwap turns a winning picture into a losing one, and a losing one into a winner.
Each tick of tmrCountdown takes one off the seconds left and shows it, and at zero both timers stop.
At zero, a message shows the score, Global.cs records that the test is taken, and the data entry form opens again.
This part makes the Take test button open the test. Then you try the whole thing.
The Take test button closes the data entry form and opens the reaction test form.
I run the program and check the name, the swaps, the score, the countdown and the way back.
Everything my program needs is done. I can pick any extra, or none.
After three wrong passwords the Login button goes grey.
One line at the top of the login code makes a counter called tries that starts at 0.
On the third wrong try, a message shows and the Login button goes grey.
I type a wrong password three times and the Login button goes grey.
The reaction test gets harder towards the end.
Every second the gap between swaps shrinks by a tenth of a second, down to 0.3 seconds.
I take the test and the swaps get faster as the clock runs down.
The attempts heading shows the biggest attempt as well as the average.
After the average, the attempts heading also shows the biggest of the three attempts.
I type three attempts and the heading shows the biggest one.
The group panel takes a colour that matches the group.
When the group appears, the group panel turns green, yellow or red.
I work out a group and the panel turns its colour.
